compiled_state.description:
Discovered while implementing e9d5-c850-d505-4a5a (typed reconciler mutation
payload contracts, ADR 0107). Two producers construct (inbound, create)
Mutation payloads with different shapes:

- differ.py's inbound-create path emits a FLAT dict of Jira fields (no
  wrapper key): {f: v for f, v in jira_fields.items() if f not in excluded}.
- binding_walk.py's ADOPT path emits a nested shape:
  {"fields": _fields, "jira_fields": _fields}.

apply_inbound.py's _apply_inbound_create leaf already explicitly tolerates
BOTH shapes (fields = payload.get("fields") or payload), which is how this
has stayed silently correct in production. ADR 0107's typed
InboundCreatePayload contract picks the flat shape (differ.py's) as
canonical, per e9d5's own corpus/contract decision -- so binding_walk.py's
nested shape would fail typed validation today.

This is a pre-existing inconsistency, NOT introduced by e9d5 -- e9d5 only
documents it (see the corpus README and e9d5's ticket comment recording
approved intentional deltas) and does not reconcile it, since producer
rewiring is ADR 0107's deferred "Cut" step and out of e9d5's own scope (AC7).

Suggested follow-up: migrate binding_walk.py's ADOPT path to emit the flat
shape (matching differ.py and the ADR 0107 InboundCreatePayload contract),
then simplify apply_inbound.py's _apply_inbound_create leaf to drop its
dual-shape tolerance, before any producer is rewired to construct
InboundCreatePayload directly (that "Cut" step is a separate, later
ticket).

Acceptance criteria:
- binding_walk.py's ADOPT path and differ.py's inbound-create path agree on
  payload shape, verified by a test asserting both producers emit the same
  normalized shape for an equivalent inbound create.
- apply_inbound.py's _apply_inbound_create no longer needs to tolerate two
  shapes (or, if kept for defense-in-depth, the tolerance is documented as
  intentional rather than load-bearing for a live producer).
compiled_state.title: Reconcile dual inbound-create payload shapes (differ.py flat vs binding_walk.py nested)
